questions.prompt: In DAX, how does the CALCULATE function modify evaluation?

options.text: It evaluates an expression under a modified filter context, and transitions any active row context into filter context.
It forces the formula to compute on the GPU.
It converts DAX measures into static physical columns.
It bypasses all relationship definitions in the data model.

questions.explanation: CALCULATE is the single most powerful DAX function because it overrides, merges, or clears filter context and triggers context transition.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Core Syntax and Primitives in Power BI

questions.prompt: Why is a Star Schema architecture preferred over a flat, single-table model in Power BI?

options.text: The VertiPaq tabular engine compresses columnar Dimension tables efficiently and executes single-direction relationships with minimal RAM.
Star schemas require fewer measures to be written.
Single flat tables cannot be refreshed automatically in the Power BI Service.
Power BI visual slicers do not function without star schemas.

questions.explanation: The VertiPaq in-memory engine achieves optimal dictionary encoding and memory compression when data is normalized into distinct Fact and Dimension tables.
questions.recommendedLessonTitle: Production Patterns and Resilience in Power BI

questions.prompt: Which of the following represent requirements for a dedicated Date Dimension in Power BI to support time-intelligence functions?

options.text: It must contain continuous calendar dates with zero gaps across the required span
It must contain at least one column formatted as Date or DateTime
It must be marked as the official Date Table in the data model
It must be stored in a SQL database rather than imported into Power BI

questions.explanation: Time intelligence (DATESYTD, SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR) requires a marked, contiguous Date table with no missing calendar days.

questions.prompt: A report visual crashes with a '#DIV/0!' visual error. Which DAX function avoids this issue cleanly?
questions.explanation: DIVIDE safely checks for zero or blank denominators and returns an optional fallback (defaulting to BLANK or 0) rather than raising an error.
